plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the named components and coordinate geometry of the pinhole camera model. A box representing the camera body is shown in 3D, with the pinhole/camera center marked as a black dot on its rear face. From this center, three axes extend: Z along the optical axis pointing forward, Y pointing upward, and X pointing laterally, forming a right-handed coordinate frame. The projection plane is labeled on the front face of the box, and the focal length f is indicated in red as the distance from that plane back to the pinhole. This figure establishes the standard naming conventions — optical center, optical axis, projection plane, and focal length — that underpin all subsequent formulations of perspective projection.

elements: semi-transparent pinhole camera body as an oblique rectangular box
projection plane as the large left/front rectangular face of the camera body
light blue-gray upper/top face of the camera box
pale olive lower/front face of the camera box
dark green right/rear side face of the camera box
black elliptical pinhole / camera center on the right side face
Z-axis arrow starting at the pinhole and extending horizontally to the right along the optical / principal axis
Y-axis arrow passing upward through the pinhole
X-axis arrow starting at the pinhole and extending diagonally upward-right into the receding direction
large axis labels X, Y, and Z near their arrowheads
label 'World coordinates' above the coordinate axes
label 'Pinhole camera' at upper left
label 'Projection plane' on the left with a curved gray callout arrow to the plane
label 'Optical / principal axis' on the right with a gray callout arrow to the Z-axis line
label 'Pinhole / camera center' below-right with a gray callout arrow to the black pinhole
red double-headed dimension arrow below the camera box indicating focal length f
italic red or black label f centered below the red dimension arrow
dashed dark-gray hidden/guide line along the left vertical edge of the projection plane
dashed dark-gray receding guide line across the top-left edge of the box
dashed dark-gray vertical center guide line on the projection plane
dashed dark-gray diagonal guide line across the lower projection-plane face
small equation readout panel showing the current handedness convention and image-coordinate sign relationship
click highlight halo or outline for the currently selected labeled component

interactions.teaches: The X, Y, and Z axes are a single camera-coordinate frame attached to the pinhole; rotating the view preserves their mutual orientation while the projection plane, optical axis, and labels stay anchored to the same physical parts

interactions.label: Coordinate convention
interactions.teaches: Flipping one image/camera axis changes the coordinate-system handedness and changes the sign interpretation of image coordinates without moving the pinhole or focal-length distance
Selecting the optical center, optical axis, projection plane, or focal length connects each named geometric part to its role in the pinhole projection equations

demo_steps.title: Right-handed camera frame
demo_steps.narration: The default view matches the figure: +Z follows the optical axis to the right, +Y points upward, and +X is the receding diagonal axis. The pinhole is the origin of the camera-coordinate frame.

demo_steps.title: Left-handed image convention
demo_steps.narration: Switching conventions flips the affected vertical image/camera axis while the pinhole, optical axis, projection plane, and focal length remain fixed. The equation readout updates to show the corresponding sign change for image coordinates.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique drawing style matching the source: +Z maps mostly screen-right, +Y maps screen-up, and +X maps along the receding diagonal upward-right. Camera body is a rectangular prism with world dimensions X depth = 1.25 units, Y height = 2.6 units, Z length/focal distance = 2.4 units. Place the pinhole/camera center at world origin (0, 0, 0) on the right/rear side face. The projection plane is the rectangular plane at Z = -f with f = 2.4, spanning X from -0.65 to +0.65 and Y from -1.3 to +1.3. The visible box extends from Z = -2.4 to Z = 0. The projection plane should appear to the left of the pinhole, with the optical axis extending from the pinhole toward +Z on the right, as in the source. Draw Z-axis from (0,0,0) to (0,0,2.8), Y-axis from (0,-0.05,0) to (0,2.15,0), and X-axis from (0,0,0) to (1.7,1.35,0) visually along the receding diagonal. In the source palette, top/projection surfaces are muted blue-gray #a9b8bb at about 0.75 opacity, lower/front face is pale olive #9fa98f at about 0.85 opacity, right side face is dark desaturated green #394938, axis and text color is near-black #101216, guide lines are dark blue-gray #435258, callout arrows are gray-blue #73888d, and focal-length arrow is bright red #ff1515. The red f arrow lies below the box, parallel to the visible Z/focal-distance span from the projection plane side toward the pinhole side. The equation readout should show for the physical projection plane drawn behind the pinhole: x = -f X/Z and y = -f Y/Z; optionally note that the common virtual image plane in front uses x = f X/Z and y = f Y/Z. For the left-handed convention, flip the displayed +Y/image-y direction downward and update the sign note accordingly.
interactionPlan.notes: Render text labels as screen-facing billboards anchored to their 3D targets so orbiting keeps labels attached but readable. Use fat lines or tube geometry for axes and callout arrows; use dashed LineSegments for hidden/guide lines. The handedness toggle should animate the affected axis flipping through the origin and update the equation panel, not move the camera body. Clicking a component should add a yellow or cyan outline/halo and show a compact tooltip: optical center = origin and ray intersection point; optical axis = Z direction/principal ray; projection plane = where rays intersect to form image coordinates; focal length f = distance from pinhole to projection plane and scale factor in projection.

discrepancies: The camera body proportions differ: the generated box is more compact and square, with a much narrower dark side face than the source's deeper oblique camera volume.
The X and Y axis labels and arrows are crowded near the 'World coordinates' label, making the world-coordinate annotation less like the spacious source layout.
The projection plane/translucent blue geometry is simplified and does not match the source's larger, more distinct blue plane extending behind/above the front face.
The pinhole/camera-center callout is lower and less prominent than in the source, and its arrow leader is thinner and less visually faithful.
Extra UI, equation readout, and handedness convention controls add concepts not present in the original static figure.
evaluation.notes: The figure is clearly recognizable and captures the main pinhole camera geometry, labels, axes, colors, and focal-length arrow, but proportions and the projection-plane/body depth relationship are noticeably simplified and extra convention/equation content goes beyond the source.
action_items: Increase the oblique depth of the camera body so the dark side face and top face more closely match the source proportions.
Make the translucent projection plane larger and more visually distinct from the front face, matching its source placement and extent.
Reposition the X, Y, and World coordinates labels to reduce crowding and better match the original composition.
Strengthen and reposition the pinhole/camera-center callout arrow and label to match the source emphasis.
plan_action_items: Remove or de-emphasize the handedness/equation interaction if the goal is strict reproduction of the textbook figure rather than an expanded teaching widget.

feedback.rationale: The figure is faithful and usable with all scores at 4, and the remaining issues are mostly proportion/layout polish plus minor extra controls rather than core conceptual or implementation failures.
